what_it_does: This paper tackles a problem with MRAM (magnetic RAM—a type of non-volatile memory that uses magnetic states to store data) used for computing directly inside memory. The issue is that standard MRAM struggles to clearly distinguish between stored +1 and -1 weights, leading to read errors and sensitivity to manufacturing variations. The solution uses two cross-coupled magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJ—the magnetic storage elements) per memory cell to store both +1 and its opposite -1 simultaneously, dramatically improving the signal strength (8100x current ratio) and making reads more robust. This is like using stereo speakers instead of mono to make the signal clearer.
